name: fmt
one_liner: A free code library that lets C++ programmers turn numbers, dates, and text into nicely formatted output faster and more safely than the old built-in tools.
buyer: There isn't really a buyer here in the ordinary sense — this is deep developer infrastructure that C++ teams pull into their own products for free; no non-technical business would ever purchase it directly.
business_use_cases: A game studio uses it internally to format debug logs and in-game text faster, but this never becomes a customer-facing product on its own.
A trading firm's C++ backend uses it for fast, correct number formatting in performance-critical systems, again purely as internal infrastructure.
A hardware/firmware vendor bundles it into an SDK, but the value is in the SDK, not this library.

money_ideas.idea: None realistic. It's permissively-licensed core infrastructure; monetizing it directly (support contracts) is a niche play only a maintainer with deep reputation could pull off.

steal_this: Nothing to build this weekend from this repo alone — it's a dependency, not a product. If anything, use it inside a C++ project you're already building.
